Each primitive represents a distinct yet interdependent facet of performance under stress. Resilience optimization (R) is a function of time and punishment tolerance (P), modeled as R(T,P). Adversity tolerance (A) and fight-through capacity (F) define a constraint surface such that A/F determines operational limits. Punishment resilience (P) modulates smile rate (S) and whistle blow status (W), forming a feedback loop. The system's stability hinges on maintaining S > 0 and W = 0 until final signal. Failure modes occur when P exceeds thresholds, causing R to collapse, A to overwhelm F, or S to drop below baseline. These primitives are mathematically dual in their functional roles, each contributing to a unified model of strategic endurance.
